summary: Authors may use generative AI tools with human oversight, but must declare their use in a dedicated statement placed before the reference list at first submission. Basic grammar, spelling and reference checkers and accessibility-only assistive tools need no disclosure, and AI cannot be listed as an author. Reviewers and editors may not upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools, but may use AI in a supportive way to polish review reports or decision letters or to run background literature searches. AI may support explanatory images and data-derived visualizations, but not primary research images.

evidence.quote: AI tools may only be applied with human oversight and control.
Authors must declare the use of generative AI tools in the manuscript preparation process upon submission of the paper.
The declaration does not apply to the use of basic tools, such as tools used to check grammar, spelling, and references.
authors must not list or cite AI tools as an author or co-author on the manuscript
AI tools must not be used to create or alter images that represent primary observed or experimental data
AI tools may be used to support the creation of explanatory images (such as flow charts, conceptual diagrams, or schematic illustrations).
this journal does not currently allow academic editors and reviewers to upload an unpublished manuscript into a generative AI tool
AI tools may be used in a supportive capacity by editors and reviewers to improve structure and language of the review report
or to conduct a background literature search.
